entry.title: Stanford Energy Seminar | AI, energy, and sustainability: from innovation to impact

media:group.media:title: Stanford Energy Seminar | AI, energy, and sustainability: from innovation to impact
media:group.media:description:
Artificial intelligence and energy are becoming deeply intertwined. AI is driving new demand for power, and it is also emerging as a powerful tool for making energy systems cleaner, more reliable, and more efficient. What does that two-way relationship look like in practice, and where is it heading?
Speaker Bio: Join us for a fireside chat with Richard Newell, former Chief Technology Officer (CTO), Sustainability Solutions, C3 AI, in conversation with John Weyant, Stanford professor and longtime leader in energy and climate systems analysis. Drawing on decades studying energy technology and markets and recent experience in enterprise AI, Newell will explore: • How different forms of AI are improving energy systems, with concrete examples • What “physical AI” is and what it could mean for the grid, infrastructure, and industry • How AI is reshaping the software industry, and what it takes for companies to deploy AI successfully • Where investors and emerging companies see the most promising opportunities at the AI-energy intersection • Lessons from earlier energy transformations that can help us make sense of this one
The conversation will also turn to what to watch in the years ahead and how students and early-career professionals can prepare to contribute. Whether you are a student, researcher, practitioner, or simply curious about where AI and energy meet, this session offers an informed, practical look at the road from innovation to impact.

entry.title: Stanford Energy Seminar | Powering what’s next: Real estate’s role in the energy transition

media:group.media:title: Stanford Energy Seminar | Powering what’s next: Real estate’s role in the energy transition
media:group.media:description:
The buildings that move the world’s goods are becoming an essential part of how we power it. Join Susan Uthayakumar, Chief Energy & Sustainability Officer at Prologis, in conversation with William Chueh, Director of the Precourt Institute for Energy, for a look at how a global leader in logistics real estate is scaling energy solutions to meet growing power demand, strengthen resilience, and advance decarbonization.
Speaker Bio: Susan Uthayakumar serves as the Managing Director, Chief Energy and Sustainability Officer and Executive Committee Member at Prologis, where she leads the company’s Energy Solutions business. In this role, she oversees the development and deployment of solutions that help customers achieve energy independence through distributed energy resources, fleet electrification, and strategic energy management. As a member of the company’s executive management team, Susan ensures alignment with Prologis’ broader business objectives and growth strategy. With a focus on scaling energy and mobility solutions, Susan plays a key role in optimizing Prologis’ assets to drive long-term value for customers. Her leadership has helped position Prologis as a global leader in providing innovative energy and mobility infrastructure within logistics real estate.
Prior to joining Prologis, Susan held various leadership positions at Schneider Electric, most recently serving as president of the Global Sustainability Business Division, where she was responsible for advancing decarbonization and energy management solutions for global customers. She also served as CEO of Schneider Electric Canada, where she led the company’s transition to a digital power and automation technology leader.
Susan has also led mergers and acquisitions at McCain Foods Limited, a global leader in the frozen food industry, and has held leadership positions at Deloitte, a global advisory firm.
She holds an Executive MBA from the Kellogg School of Management at Northwestern University, focusing on international business practices, along with a Master of Accounting (MAcc) and a Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Waterloo. Susan has also completed the Board Certification Program at Stanford and holds the Chartered Accountant (CA) and Certified Public Accountant (CPA) designations.

entry.title: Stanford Energy Seminar | The renewables reckoning

media:group.media:title: Stanford Energy Seminar | The renewables reckoning
media:group.media:description:
The U.S. renewable energy industry is in the midst of a financial crisis. Over the past 18 months, more than 100 companies have filed for bankruptcy, even as solar accounted for roughly 80% of new U.S. electricity generation last year. In this seminar, Nick Franchot of GoodFinch will explain what is driving the wave of distress and what it reveals about how the industry has been financed.
Speaker Bio: Franchot will also discuss GoodFinch's strategy of acquiring assets out of bankruptcy, which has produced one of the largest renewable energy portfolios in the country, with more than $1 billion in EBITDA and close to 1% of U.S. power production. He will close with the implications for the U.S. economy: if, as GoodFinch expects, half of the developers behind recent solar growth fail in the coming years, new energy supply could be significantly constrained at a moment of rising demand.
Nick Franchot is currently a Partner at GoodFinch. Nick brings experience from previous roles at Hall Capital Partners LLC, Passport Capital, U.S. Department of the Treasury and CapitalSource. He holds a Stanford University Graduate School of Business

entry.title: Stanford Energy Seminar | Improving decisions for U.S. electricity under policy uncertainty

media:group.media:title: Stanford Energy Seminar | Improving decisions for U.S. electricity under policy uncertainty
media:group.media:description:
The United States needs to build generation, storage, and transmission infrastructure to meet growing electricity demand. However, there is a lack of decision tools and frameworks to inform investment decisions for energy technologies amid policy, technological, and other contextual uncertainties. Prof. Azevedo will present results from several ongoing analyses that quantify the costs, benefits, and technology investments needed across the country for a variety of policy and technology scenarios (such as the need for transmission expansion under different policy contexts; the effects of increased load from data centers; the opportunities for enhanced geothermal, small modular nuclear reactors, storage technologies, and offshore wind, just to name a few, as well as the effect of different climate futures on optimal investment decisions). Prof. Azevedo uses a new modeling and data tool that has been developed by her group, PyPSA-USA, that includes characteristics of generators, transmission, candidate new generation and transmission technologies, a representation of renewable generation potential, and state- and federal-level policies and incentives.
Speaker Bio: Inês Azevedo is professor of Energy Science & Engineering at Stanford University. Her work focuses on how to transition to sustainable, realistically feasible, and equitable energy systems. She is passionate about solving problems that include environmental, technical, economic, and policy issues, where traditional engineering approaches play an important role but cannot provide a complete answer. In particular, she is interested in assessing how energy systems are likely to evolve, which requires comprehensive knowledge of the technologies that can address future energy needs and the decision-making process followed by various agents in the economy.

entry.title: Stanford Energy Seminar | AI for climate solutions

media:group.media:title: Stanford Energy Seminar | AI for climate solutions
media:group.media:description:
GRAIL — the Green Artificial Intelligence Learning network — is a global collaboration platform, founded by the Nand & Jeet Khemka Foundation, built to close the gap between two communities that rarely work together: the people building frontier AI and the people running the climate systems that need to decarbonise. Promising AI capability too often fails to convert into deployed outcomes because there is no translation layer between them. GRAIL is that layer to bring AI solutions to transform applied domains including energy, materials, value chains and the built environment to create economic value and deliver climate impact.
Speaker Bio: Shanthakumar Bannirchelvam is a Director of the Sustainable and AI investing teams at the SUN Group, a 120-year-old business group and Single Family Office which has established leading asset managers including Sequoia Capital India (now Peak XV Partners). Prior to this role, he worked at Nomura Greentech in their sustainable investment banking division, where he advised on infrastructure and energy transition deals.
He has also previously worked in corporate law in Sydney and London with Herbert Smith Freehills, the United Nations Economic and Social Council in New York and served as an Infantry Officer in the Singapore Armed Forces. Shanthakumar is admitted to practice in the Supreme Court of NSW and holds a Bachelor of Laws / Bachelor of Economics from the University of Sydney and an MBA from Columbia Business School, where he was a Three Cairns Climate Fellow.

entry.title: Postdocs cracking open the black box of catalysis | Stanford Energy Fellowship

media:group.media:title: Postdocs cracking open the black box of catalysis | Stanford Energy Fellowship
media:group.media:description:
Stanford Energy Postdoctoral Fellows Kang Rui Garrick Lim and Zisheng "ZZ" Zhang team up to study a two-metal catalyst that turns carbon dioxide into methanol. Garrick works in the lab; ZZ uses computer simulations. Together, they're figuring out how the catalyst works and how to turn a greenhouse gas into one of the world's most important chemicals.
